facts.text: Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons) was deployed at Gale Crater during Curiosity (MSL) in 2014.

Rising 5.5 km above the crater floor, Mount Sharp is a layered mountain of sedimentary rock. Each layer records a chapter of Mars's environmental history. As Curiosity climbs, it reads that history: from clay-rich layers (wet era) through sulphate layers (drying era) to dry oxidised layers at the top. It is a geological time machine.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Its layered sedimentary rock records billions of years of Martian climate change — from a wet, habitable world to the cold, dry planet we see today.
Mount Sharp is Curiosity's ongoing destination; the rover continues to climb and read Mars's environmental history layer by layer.
